chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I am your ransom, these two companions of mine did not know to stand at Al-Muzdalifah.' He said: 'They return to their place and stand at Al-Mash'ar for an hour.' I said: 'No one informed them until that day, and the people had already departed.' He lowered his head for a moment, then said: 'Did they not pray the morning prayer at Al-Muzdalifah?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Did they not perform Qunut in their prayer?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Their Hajj is complete.' Then he said: 'Al-Mash'ar is part of Al-Muzdalifah, and Al-Muzdalifah is part of Al-Mash'ar, and a little supplication suffices for them.'

key_terms.المَشْعَر: Al-Mash'ar, referring to Al-Mash'ar al-Haram (the Sacred Monument) at Al-Muzdalifah
key_terms.المُزْدَلِفَة: Al-Muzdalifah, a plain near Mecca where pilgrims stand after leaving Mina

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim misses standing at Al-Muzdalifah due to ignorance?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the principle of *rukhsah* (concession) by validating the Hajj of companions who missed the formal standing at Al-Mash'ar due to ignorance, provided they had prayed Fajr in Al-Muzdalifah. The Imam clarifies the geographical and ritual interchangeability of Al-Muzdalifah and Al-Mash'ar, emphasizing that the core requirement is the act of standing and supplication rather than a rigid location, thus highlighting the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding ritual obligations.
